sentences.text: This is Second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No781/2024 dated 31/05/2024 registered at Police Station Kolgawan, District Satna (M.P) for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(cha), 376(3), 506 of IPC and Sections 4 and 5 of POCSO Act.

Earlier application was dismissed on merit vide order dated 22/08/2024 in M.Cr.C.
No.32503/2024.
2.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that statements of the prosecutirx and her mother have also been recorded and though both the witnesses have made an attempt to support the prosecution story but the fact remains that the report in regard to incident dated 26/04/2024 has been lodged on 31/05/2024 with the delay of more than a month.
There is no proper explanation regarding the delay which occasioned in lodging of FIR.

According to paragraph 2 of the testimony of the prosecutrix reflects that she had disclosed the incident to her mother after two-three days but no report has been lodged for more than a month, hence, the applicant who is aged about 19 years and is in custody since 01.06.2024 having no criminal past deserves to be enlarged on bail.

3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the prayer and submitted that the prosecutrix and her mother, have supported the allegation levelled against the applicant, therefore,
he is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: 4. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
5. A perusal of the case diary it reflects that the FIR has been lodged after more than a month from the date of incident and the DNA report is negative.
The applicant is aged about 19 years is in custody since 01.06.2024 and has no criminal past.
6. Thus, taking into consideration the totality of the circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered view that it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant-Ravendra @ Chhotoo Dahiya shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that the applicants shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
9.
Accordingly, M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE Astha Ravendra @ Chhotoo Dahiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105702864/
